items.q: Hoover sign positive in leg weakness indicates what?
items.exp: Involuntary hip extension synergising with contralateral hip flexion reveals preserved power in functional weakness. It is a rule in positive sign, though organic disease must still be excluded appropriately.
r: Incorrect. Stroke weakness lacks this synergy pattern.
Correct. Hoover sign means functional weakness.
Incorrect. Myasthenia fatigues without Hoover pattern.
Incorrect. Cord signs include sphincter and level findings.
items.kp: Leg extends when other flexes: functional.

items.q: Somatic symptom disorder diagnosis principally requires what?
o: Distressing symptoms plus excessive thoughts, feelings and behaviours about them over 6 months
items.exp: DSM shifted from medically unexplained to maladaptive response: symptoms (explained or not) with disproportionate persistent thoughts, high health anxiety and excessive time or energy devoted, causing impairment.
r: Incorrect. Medical disease may coexist.
Correct. Excessive response over six months.
Incorrect. Faking defines factitious or malingering.
Incorrect. Tests may be abnormal from comorbid disease.
items.kp: It is the excess worry, not missing cause.

items.q: Persistent feeling of being detached observer of oneself, world seems unreal, yet knows it is only a feeling. Diagnosis?
items.exp: Depersonalisation (self detached) and derealisation (world unreal) with intact reality testing define this dissociative disorder, often anxiety and trauma linked, distinct from psychotic loss of insight.
r: Incorrect. Reality testing intact excludes psychosis.
Correct. Depersonalisation derealisation disorder.
Incorrect. No identity alteration with amnesia.
Incorrect. Cognition otherwise preserved.
items.kp: Feels unreal but knows better: depersonalisation.

items.q: Mother repeatedly brings child with fabricated apnoea episodes occurring only with her, investigations normal. This is what and needs what?
o: Factitious disorder imposed on another; safeguarding referral
items.exp: Caregiver falsification (factitious imposed on another) abuses the victim through presentations and procedures; child protection referral and coordinated single team care are urgent, without direct accusatory confrontation.
r: Incorrect. Child is victim, not malingerer.
Correct. Imposed factitious disorder, safeguard child.
Incorrect. Victim focused abuse pattern dominates.
Incorrect. Fabricated episodes are abuse.
items.kp: Fabricated child illness equals safeguard now.

items.q: Malingering is distinguished from factitious disorder by what?
items.exp: Both intentionally produce symptoms, but malingering seeks external gain (compensation, avoiding work or prosecution) while factitious seeks internal sick role. Neither is diagnosed lightly; evidence must be strong.
r: Incorrect. Both are intentional by definition.
Correct. External gain equals malingering.
Incorrect. Normal tests occur in many conditions.
Incorrect. Timing does not separate them.
items.kp: Money motive means malingering; sick role means factitious.

items.q: Non epileptic (dissociative) seizures are best confirmed how when diagnosis uncertain?
o: Video EEG capturing typical event without epileptiform activity plus semiology
items.exp: Capturing habitual event on video EEG (long duration, closed eyes, asynchronous movements supportive) without epileptic discharge is gold standard, though coexistence with epilepsy occurs and needs neurology psychiatry joint care.
r: Incorrect. Routine EEG misses events and interictal norms mislead.
Correct. Video EEG of typical attack.
Incorrect. MRI normality does not prove dissociation.
Incorrect. Sedatives suppress many behaviours nonspecifically.
items.kp: Film the event with EEG running.

items.q: Man found wandering in another city unable to recall identity after traumatic event, later recovering memory, suggests what?
items.exp: Dissociative fugue (amnesia subtype) involves purposeful travel with autobiographical amnesia following trauma, with recovery typical. Dementia is progressive and delirium fluctuates with inattention.
r: Incorrect. Dementia does not remit like this.
Correct. Dissociative amnesia with fugue.
Incorrect. No psychotic syndrome described.
Incorrect. Consciousness clear, course different.
items.kp: Trauma, travel and lost identity: dissociative fugue.

items.q: Management anchor for somatic symptom disorder in primary care is what?
o: Regular scheduled reviews, validation, limited investigations and CBT, one coordinating clinician
items.exp: Scheduled (not symptom contingent) appointments, empathic validation, focus on function, restrained testing and CBT reduce doctor shopping and iatrogenesis. Dismissal destroys alliance and worsens symptoms.
r: Incorrect. Testing cascades harm.
Correct. Scheduled coordinated care plus CBT.
Incorrect. Symptoms are real suffering.
Incorrect. Fragmentation amplifies anxiety.
items.kp: Book reviews by calendar, not by symptom panic.

items.q: Illness anxiety disorder differs from somatic symptom disorder chiefly how?
o: Preoccupation with having disease despite minimal or no somatic symptoms
items.exp: Illness anxiety centres on disease conviction with slight symptoms and checking or avoidance behaviours, while somatic symptom disorder centres on distressing prominent symptoms themselves. Both need CBT and restrained reassurance testing.
r: Incorrect. Anxiety is defining.
Correct. Disease fear with minimal symptoms.
Incorrect. Faking is factitious spectrum.
Incorrect. Needs six months pattern.
items.kp: Few symptoms, huge disease fear: illness anxiety.

items.q: Sensory loss splitting exactly at midline and stopping at joint lines suggests which pattern?
items.exp: Non anatomical boundaries (exact midline split impossible from overlapping innervation, joint line cutoffs) indicate functional sensory loss, a positive pattern sign supporting functional neurological disorder alongside normal reflexes.
r: Incorrect. Dermatomes follow root maps.
Correct. Midline split means functional pattern.
Incorrect. Cord gives level and tract signs.
Incorrect. Neuropathy is glove stocking gradual.
